content: Courte, amusant, très facile ! Excellent ! Je veux juste demander, si 1 ≤ M_i ≤ 1 000 000, comment est-ce que "0 ≤ M_1 × M_2 × ⋯ × M_N < 2³²" est possible ? Ça devrait être "1 ≤ M_1 × M_2 × ⋯ × M_N < 2³²", n'est ce pas ? Ou tu peux changer 1 ≤ M_i ≤ 1 000 000 à 0 ≤ M_i ≤ 1 000 000 et ajouter un nouveux testcase. Je pense c'est mieux.

@5DN1L Since you're native english speaker, is it clear for you that "compute the last 4 digits of the product of these integers" means "get the last 4 digits of each number and compute their product"? When I tested it, at first I thought that I needed to compute the product of every number and then getting the last 4 digits of the result. I'm asking because this might have been a misinterpretation of mine.

"Compute the last 4 digits of the product of these integers" naturally means: first compute the product of the integers, and then take the last 4 digits of the result.

If the intended meaning were to take the last 4 digits of each integer first and then multiply them, the wording would have been "compute the product of the last 4 digits of these integers", but that wouldn't imply anything about the number of digits to output at the end.

So I'd say this was a misinterpretation rather than an ambiguity in the wording.

However, if the wording can cause confusion, it could be rewritten as a two-step instruction:

"Compute the product of the integers, and then output the last 4 digits of the result."

(Or for that matter, your interpretation could be similarly rewritten as:

"Take the last 4 digits of each integer, and then output their product.")

P.S. Just to clarify, I'm not a native English speaker.

Oh my god, I'm sorry for the confusion.

This wasn't a misinterpretation, it was an error in my code that was wrong but I thought it was correct.

It's all fine, actually. I'm sorry for this.
